chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Haytham al-Tamimi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: A man had with him his wife, who was unable to stand on her feet, so her husband carried her in a litter and performed with her the obligatory tawaf of the House and the sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah. Would that tawaf, his performing tawaf with her, suffice for himself as well?
So he said: "Yes indeed, by Allah, then it would."

key_terms.أَيُجْزِيهِ: would it suffice or fulfill the obligation for him
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa, one of the two stations of sa'i
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other station of sa'i
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: around the Sacred House, the Ka'bah
key_terms.صَاحِبَتُهُ: his wife or female companion in this context
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf required as part of the rite
key_terms.طَوَافُهُ بِهَا: his tawaf while carrying or accompanying her
key_terms.مَحْمِلٍ: a litter or carried seat used for transport

ai.seo_question: Does a husband's tawaf while carrying his wife count for his own obligatory tawaf too?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning tawaf during hajj or 'umrah when a man carries his incapacitated wife. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام states that the man's tawaf while carrying her suffices for his own obligatory tawaf as well. The narration relates to ritual rulings of hajj and also reflects spousal assistance in worship.
